steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control colon samples (6 vs 6, unpaired), using RSEM gene-level expected counts with control as the reference level?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test per R-0001/R-0029; minimal pre-filter per R-0002; median-of-ratios normalization inside the model per R-0026; explicit reference level and named contrast per R-0036; RSEM gene table with no per-sample genes.results/length table means the length offset is lost, stated per R-0169; Cook's distance NA-flagging behavior at n=6/group reported per R-0039

steps.description: Using the DESeqDataSet from T1S1 (rounded RSEM expected counts, no length offset available since per-sample genes.results with effective lengths were not delivered — state this explicitly as a caveat: a shift in isoform usage between conditions could appear as apparent differential expression at the gene level), apply a minimal pre-filter keeping genes with >=10 counts in >=6 samples (the smallest group size), set condition explicitly with control as the reference level, fit DESeq2's median-of-ratios size factors and negative-binomial GLM, and run the Wald test for the treated-vs-control contrast. Because each group has only 6 replicates, keep DESeq2's default Cook's-distance outlier flagging on (cells with <7 replicates get NA p-values rather than count replacement) and report which genes are flagged this way, separately from genes removed by independent filtering. Based on T1S1's finding, decide explicitly whether sample_01 is retained (default, since a low library size alone is not a removal reason) or excluded, and state the reason either way.

steps.name: apeglm shrinkage, BH multiple testing, and significance calling
steps.question: After shrinking the log2 fold change with apeglm, which genes are significantly differentially expressed at BH-adjusted p<0.05, and is the p-value histogram well-behaved?

grounding.reason: apeglm shrinkage for a single coefficient per R-0009; BH adjustment with independent filtering held at the reporting alpha per R-0166/R-0010; selection by adjusted p-value only per R-0043; p-value histogram inspected before trusting adjusted values per R-0083; MA/dispersion plots as fit diagnostics per R-0087

steps.description: Apply lfcShrink(type='apeglm') to the treated-vs-control coefficient from T1S2 to obtain a shrunken log2 fold change and its SE, keeping the unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE and Wald p-values in the table alongside the shrunken values. Plot the histogram of unadjusted p-values from results() before adjustment and inspect its shape (flat or left-decreasing is expected). plan.title: Colon treated vs control DE (RSEM) + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 colon samples (6 treated, 6 control, unpaired, single batch) were quantified with RSEM to gene-level expected counts; the per-sample genes.results files carrying effective lengths were not delivered, so no length offset can be recovered — this is fit and reported as counts without length correction (a caveat, not a blocker, since the comparison is within-gene across samples of the same protocol). Sample_01's library size is ~4x below the median, which the plan does not silently drop: sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library-size table) inspects it explicitly before any test runs, and its size factor absorbs the depth difference in the DESeq2 model. Because the RSEM counts are non-integer expected counts, they are rounded to nearest integer before DESeq2 (a negative-binomial count model requires integers). The core comparison is a standard DESeq2 Wald test (treated vs control, control as reference) with a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples), apeglm shrinkage of the log2 fold change for reporting/ranking, and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha=0.05 to call significant genes. Because n=6/group falls in the 3-6 replicate range, DESeq2 will flag (not replace) Cook's-distance count outliers as NA — these are reported explicitly. Downstream, the full ranked gene list (Wald statistic) is tested against the MSigDB Hallmark human collection and then Reactome via fgsea preranked GSEA, since a handful of coordinated small changes may not surface as individually significant genes. A final report ties DE results, QC diagnostics, and enrichment findings together with full reproducibility metadata.

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
